title: Towards Sustainable Post-Exascale Leadership Computing
problem: Post-exascale computing systems face diminishing returns in performance per watt, creating a barrier to sustaining HPC growth within strict energy budget constraints.
motivation: Energy efficiency is critical for the viability and sustainability of future leadership computing systems as silicon technology approaches its physical limits.
method: Proposes a multifaceted strategy integrating energy-aware practices across all HPC levels: system design, software development, and operational policies. Adopts application-specific accelerators, develops energy-efficient algorithms, and implements data-driven operational analytics to optimize system performance within energy budgets.
key_novelty: Comprehensive integration of energy-awareness across all layers of HPC infrastructure from hardware selection to operational management for sustainable post-exascale systems.
contributions: Multifaceted strategy for specialized hardware optimized for energy efficiency in specific applications
Integration of energy-aware practices across system design, software development, and operational policies
Strategic opportunities including application-specific accelerators and energy-efficient algorithms
Comprehensive roadmap for sustainable leadership computing systems at OLCF within energy budgets

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: performance per watt discussed qualitatively; energy budget constraints emphasized but not quantified

limitations: Not discussed; this is a strategic roadmap and vision paper rather than an empirical study with experimental validation.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient architectures for sustainable post-exascale HPC
